data.name: CompanionSetup.questionable.setup.Label
data.comment: Questionable setting name.

data.name: CompanionSetup.questionable.setup.Recommended
data.comment: Recommended value.

data.name: CompanionSetup.questionable.setup.Why
data.value: Until it is finished, /qst and Questionable's window refuse to work. Open Questionable and press Finish Setup.
data.comment: Why the setting matters.

data.name: CompanionSetup.questionable.combat-module.Label
data.comment: Questionable setting name (its own label).

data.name: CompanionSetup.questionable.combat-module.Recommended
data.value: Boss Mod, Wrath Combo or Rotation Solver Reborn (installed)
data.comment: Recommended value.

data.name: CompanionSetup.questionable.combat-module.Why
data.value: With None, every fight in a quest is left to you.
data.comment: Why the setting matters.

data.name: CompanionSetup.questionable.configure-textadvance.Label
data.value: Automatically configure TextAdvance with the recommended settings
data.comment: Questionable setting name (its own label).

data.name: CompanionSetup.questionable.configure-textadvance.Recommended
data.comment: Recommended value.

data.name: CompanionSetup.questionable.configure-textadvance.Why
data.value: Questionable then turns TextAdvance's quest accept, turn-in and dialogue on while it runs. Off, your own TextAdvance settings must do it.
data.comment: Why the setting matters.

data.name: CompanionSetup.questionable.dont-skip-cutscenes.Label
data.comment: Questionable setting name (its own label, under the TextAdvance one).

data.name: CompanionSetup.questionable.dont-skip-cutscenes.Recommended
data.comment: Recommended value.

data.name: CompanionSetup.questionable.dont-skip-cutscenes.Why
data.value: On, Questionable stops answering dialogue choices, so a run waits for you at every prompt.
data.comment: Why the setting matters.

data.name: CompanionSetup.questionable.prevent-completion.Label
data.comment: Questionable setting name.

data.name: CompanionSetup.questionable.prevent-completion.Recommended
data.comment: Recommended value.

data.name: CompanionSetup.questionable.prevent-completion.Why
data.value: On, Questionable never turns a quest in, so nothing Tsukimichi sends gets done.
data.comment: Why the setting matters.

data.name: CompanionSetup.questionable.prevent-completion.Need
data.comment: Completes CompanionSetupBlockedFormat: "Questionable needs its "Prevent quest completion" off".

data.name: CompanionSetup.questionable.stop-conditions.Label
data.value: Stop Questionable when any of the conditions below are met
data.comment: Questionable setting name (its own label).

data.name: CompanionSetup.questionable.stop-conditions.Recommended
data.value: off, or check its quest and level list
data.comment: Recommended value.

data.name: CompanionSetup.questionable.stop-conditions.Why
data.value: A run started from Tsukimichi can stop halfway at one of those quests or levels.
data.comment: Why the setting matters.

data.name: CompanionSetup.questionable.command-after-stop.Label
data.value: Run command when Questionable finishes automatic questing
data.comment: Questionable setting name (its own label).

data.name: CompanionSetup.questionable.command-after-stop.Recommended
data.comment: Recommended value.

data.name: CompanionSetup.questionable.command-after-stop.Why
data.value: Tsukimichi's Stop button runs that command too (by default /li auto, a Lifestream trip).
data.comment: Why the setting matters.

data.name: CompanionSetup.questionable.autoduty.Label
data.value: Run instanced content with AutoDuty and BossMod
data.comment: Questionable setting name (its own label).

data.name: CompanionSetup.questionable.autoduty.Recommended
data.comment: Recommended value.

data.name: CompanionSetup.questionable.autoduty.Why
data.value: Off, a quest's dungeon only opens the Duty Finder and waits for you.
data.comment: Why the setting matters.

data.name: CompanionSetup.questionable.solo-duties.Label
data.comment: Questionable setting name (its own label).

data.name: CompanionSetup.questionable.solo-duties.Recommended
data.value: on (needs Boss Mod; Boss Mod Reborn does not serve here)
data.comment: Recommended value.

data.name: CompanionSetup.questionable.solo-duties.Why
data.value: Off, a solo quest battle waits for you to play it.
data.comment: Why the setting matters.

data.name: CompanionSetup.textadvance.quest-accept.Label
data.comment: TextAdvance setting name (its own label).

data.name: CompanionSetup.textadvance.quest-accept.Recommended
data.comment: Recommended value.

data.name: CompanionSetup.textadvance.quest-accept.Why
data.value: Questionable accepts quests through TextAdvance; off, it stops at every quest offer.
data.comment: Why the setting matters.

data.name: CompanionSetup.textadvance.quest-accept.Need
data.comment: Completes CompanionSetupBlockedFormat: "Questionable needs TextAdvance's quest accept on".

data.name: CompanionSetup.textadvance.quest-complete.Label
data.comment: TextAdvance setting name (its own label).

data.name: CompanionSetup.textadvance.quest-complete.Recommended
data.comment: Recommended value.

data.name: CompanionSetup.textadvance.quest-complete.Why
data.value: Questionable turns quests in through TextAdvance; off, it stops at every turn-in.
data.comment: Why the setting matters.

data.name: CompanionSetup.textadvance.quest-complete.Need
data.comment: Completes CompanionSetupBlockedFormat.

data.name: CompanionSetup.textadvance.talk-skip.Label
data.comment: TextAdvance setting name (its own label).

data.name: CompanionSetup.textadvance.talk-skip.Recommended
data.comment: Recommended value.

data.name: CompanionSetup.textadvance.talk-skip.Why
data.value: Off, every conversation in a Questionable run waits for a click.
data.comment: Why the setting matters.

data.name: CompanionSetup.textadvance.enabled.Label
data.comment: TextAdvance setting name (its own label).

data.name: CompanionSetup.textadvance.enabled.Recommended
data.value: on (add the character to its auto-enable list so it stays on after logging in)
data.comment: Recommended value.

data.name: CompanionSetup.textadvance.enabled.Why
data.value: TextAdvance turns itself off at logout; while it is off, nothing is accepted or turned in.
data.comment: Why the setting matters.

data.name: CompanionSetup.textadvance.not-paused.Label
data.comment: TextAdvance state (its red "stopped by these plugins" banner).

data.name: CompanionSetup.textadvance.not-paused.Recommended
data.comment: Recommended value.

data.name: CompanionSetup.textadvance.not-paused.Why
data.value: While another plugin holds TextAdvance stopped (its window names it), even Questionable's runs wait at dialogue.
data.comment: Why the setting matters.

data.name: CompanionSetup.autoduty.manage-rotation.Label
data.comment: AutoDuty setting name (its own label).

data.name: CompanionSetup.autoduty.manage-rotation.Recommended
data.comment: Recommended value.

data.name: CompanionSetup.autoduty.manage-rotation.Why
data.value: Off, AutoDuty never turns your rotation on and the character does not attack. AutoDuty turns this off itself when Wrath Combo refuses it.
data.comment: Why the setting matters.

data.name: CompanionSetup.autoduty.alternative-rotation.Label
data.comment: AutoDuty setting name (its own label).

data.name: CompanionSetup.autoduty.alternative-rotation.Recommended
data.comment: Recommended value.

data.name: CompanionSetup.autoduty.alternative-rotation.Why
data.value: On, AutoDuty leaves the rotation entirely to you.
data.comment: Why the setting matters.

data.name: CompanionSetup.autoduty.wrath-setup-jobs.Label
data.comment: AutoDuty setting name (its own label).

data.name: CompanionSetup.autoduty.wrath-setup-jobs.Recommended
data.comment: Recommended value.

data.name: CompanionSetup.autoduty.wrath-setup-jobs.Why
data.value: Off, a job you have not set up in Wrath Combo gets no rotation from it.
data.comment: Why the setting matters.

data.name: CompanionSetup.autoduty.manage-bossmod.Label
data.comment: AutoDuty setting name (its own label).

data.name: CompanionSetup.autoduty.manage-bossmod.Recommended
data.comment: Recommended value.

data.name: CompanionSetup.autoduty.manage-bossmod.Why
data.value: Off, AutoDuty sets no Boss Mod preset: the character neither dodges nor follows the party.
data.comment: Why the setting matters.

data.name: CompanionSetup.autoduty.leave-duty.Label
data.value: Auto Leave Duty in last loop
data.comment: AutoDuty setting name (its own label).

data.name: CompanionSetup.autoduty.leave-duty.Recommended
data.comment: Recommended value.

data.name: CompanionSetup.autoduty.leave-duty.Why
data.value: Off, the run ends with you still inside the duty.
data.comment: Why the setting matters.

data.name: CompanionSetup.autoduty.block-leaving.Label
data.value: Block leaving duty until it's complete
data.comment: AutoDuty setting name (its own label).

data.name: CompanionSetup.autoduty.block-leaving.Recommended
data.comment: Recommended value.

data.name: CompanionSetup.autoduty.block-leaving.Why
data.value: On, a path that ends before the duty is done never leaves.
data.comment: Why the setting matters.

data.name: CompanionSetup.autoduty.unsynced.Label
data.comment: AutoDuty setting name (its own label).

data.name: CompanionSetup.autoduty.unsynced.Recommended
data.comment: Recommended value.

data.name: CompanionSetup.autoduty.unsynced.Why
data.value: On, a Duty Finder run queues unsynced and takes the path's unsynced steps.
data.comment: Why the setting matters.

data.name: CompanionSetup.lifestream.firmament.Label
data.value: Add firmament location into Foundation aetheryte
data.comment: Lifestream setting name (its own label).

data.name: CompanionSetup.lifestream.firmament.Recommended
data.comment: Recommended value.

data.name: CompanionSetup.lifestream.firmament.Why
data.value: Off, Go to giver's hop from the Foundation to the Firmament goes nowhere.
data.comment: Why the setting matters.

data.name: CompanionSetup.lifestream.custom-overrides.Label
data.value: Allow custom alias and house alias to override built-in commands
data.comment: Lifestream setting name (its own label).

data.name: CompanionSetup.lifestream.custom-overrides.Recommended
data.comment: Recommended value.

data.name: CompanionSetup.lifestream.custom-overrides.Why
data.value: On, an alias named "island" or "occult" replaces the trips Teleport takes to those quest givers.
data.comment: Why the setting matters.

data.name: CompanionSetup.vnavmesh.auto-load.Label
data.value: Automatically load/build navigation data when changing zones
data.comment: vnavmesh setting name (its own label).

data.name: CompanionSetup.vnavmesh.auto-load.Recommended
data.comment: Recommended value.

data.name: CompanionSetup.vnavmesh.auto-load.Why
data.value: Off, the map is never loaded after a zone change and Walk to giver waits at "Preparing path…".
data.comment: Why the setting matters.

data.name: CompanionSetup.vnavmesh.auto-load.Need
data.comment: Completes CompanionSetupBlockedFormat: "vnavmesh needs its automatic navigation loading on".

data.name: CompanionSetup.artisan.gearsets.Label
data.value: A saved gear set for each crafter
data.comment: Artisan requirement (not a setting).

data.name: CompanionSetup.artisan.gearsets.Recommended
data.value: save one gear set per crafting class in the game's Gear Set list
data.comment: The step to take.

data.name: CompanionSetup.artisan.gearsets.Why
data.value: Craft switches to the recipe's crafter through its gear set, and stops when there is none.
data.comment: Why it matters.

data.name: CompanionSetup.artisan.exit-stance.Label
data.comment: Artisan setting name (its own label).

data.name: CompanionSetup.artisan.exit-stance.Recommended
data.comment: Recommended value.

data.name: CompanionSetup.artisan.exit-stance.Why
data.value: Off, the character stays at the crafting log after the craft and cannot walk to the turn-in.
data.comment: Why the setting matters.

data.name: CompanionSetup.artisan.stop-nq.Label
data.value: Disable Endurance Mode Upon Crafting an NQ item
data.comment: Artisan setting name (its own label).

data.name: CompanionSetup.artisan.stop-nq.Recommended
data.comment: Recommended value.

data.name: CompanionSetup.artisan.stop-nq.Why
data.value: On, Craft can stop short of the amount the quest asks for.
data.comment: Why the setting matters.

data.name: CompanionSetup.artisan.stop-fail.Label
data.value: Disable Endurance Mode Upon Failed Craft
data.comment: Artisan setting name (its own label).

data.name: CompanionSetup.artisan.stop-fail.Recommended
data.comment: Recommended value.

data.name: CompanionSetup.artisan.stop-fail.Why
data.value: On, one failed craft stops the rest of the amount.
data.comment: Why the setting matters.

data.name: CompanionSetup.gatherbuddy.teleport.Label
data.comment: GatherBuddy setting name (its own label).

data.name: CompanionSetup.gatherbuddy.teleport.Recommended
data.comment: Recommended value.

data.name: CompanionSetup.gatherbuddy.teleport.Why
data.value: Off, Gather only marks the node and you travel there yourself.
data.comment: Why the setting matters.

data.name: CompanionSetup.gatherbuddy.set-names.Label
data.comment: GatherBuddy setting name (its own label).

data.name: CompanionSetup.gatherbuddy.set-names.Recommended
data.value: the names of your own gathering gear sets
data.comment: The step to take.

data.name: CompanionSetup.gatherbuddy.set-names.Why
data.value: GatherBuddy changes gear by gear set name; a name that does not match fails with a chat error. GatherBuddy Reborn picks the set by job instead.
data.comment: Why the setting matters.

data.name: CompanionSetup.allagantools.open-once.Label
data.value: Retainers, saddlebags, armoire and glamour dresser opened once
data.comment: Allagan Tools requirement (not a setting).

data.name: CompanionSetup.allagantools.open-once.Recommended
data.value: open each once on every character
data.comment: The step to take.

data.name: CompanionSetup.allagantools.open-once.Why
data.value: Allagan Tools counts what they hold only after it has seen them open; until then the Hand in counts leave them out.
data.comment: Why it matters.

data.name: Help.TopicLede.QuickStart

data.name: Help.TopicLede.Filters

data.name: Help.TopicLede.ReadingAQuest

data.name: Help.TopicLede.Moonlit

data.name: Help.TopicLede.Characters
data.value: One snapshot per character keeps the whole account in view, even logged out.

data.name: Help.TopicLede.Flight
data.value: Which quests stand between you and flying, and what you can start where you are.

data.name: Help.TopicLede.Plan
data.value: Every blue unlock quest you have left, in the order the story reaches them.

data.name: Help.TopicLede.Companions

data.comment: One-line summary of the companion plugins.

data.name: Help.TopicLede.Commands
data.value: Everything the chat command can do.

data.name: Help.TopicLede.CountsDiffer
data.value: Four reasons a done/total here is not the number in the game's journal or on a wiki.

data.name: Help.TopicLede.KnownQuirks
data.value: Things the plugin gets wrong on purpose or cannot know yet, so you need not report them.

data.name: Help.TopicLede.Spoilers
data.value: The spoiler shield keeps the story ahead of you out of sight, on by default.

data.name: Help.TopicLede.Tips
data.value: Small habits that make the catalog faster.

data.name: Help.StepOpenBody
data.value: Type /tsukimichi or /tsuki, or pick Tsukimichi in the plugin list. The tabs run down the left edge beside the journal tree, the quest table sits in the middle and the detail pane on the right.

data.name: Help.StepFindTitle
data.value: Find what you can do now

data.name: Help.StepFindBody
data.value: Search by quest, reward or id (Ctrl+F), or pick a quick view on the toolbar: Unlocks, My level, Stalled, Story sidequests or Sprout mode. All turns the view off.

data.name: Help.StepFiltersBody
data.value: Filters opens a drawer over the tree; the number on the button counts the filters narrowing the table. Each one shows as a chip in the line over the list, and the list's title names the tree scope with an × to clear it; click a chip to clear it.

data.name: Help.StepReadTitle
data.value: Read why a quest is locked

data.name: Help.StepReadBody
data.value: Select a row: the detail pane lists every requirement and marks the one that blocks you, and the Status column says it in one clause. The moon's shape is its state.

data.name: Help.StepMoonlitBody
data.value: The Moonlit tab lists quests whose reward exists nowhere else, grouped by kind, with whether you already have each one.

data.name: Help.StepCharactersBody
data.value: The Characters tab keeps a snapshot per character. Pick one to browse the whole catalog as that character, with a dashboard of its progress.

data.name: Help.StepFlightBody
data.value: The Flight tab lists every zone you can fly in. Pick one to see its quest currents, the quest that blocks each and where to fly next.

data.name: Help.StepPlanBody
data.value: The My blues tab lists every blue unlock quest you have left, by expansion and zone, with what each one unlocks. Copy it as a checklist, or pin an expansion to the Todo overlay.

data.name: Help.StepTourBody
data.value: The tour has three short chapters, Find, Read and Beyond, each pointing at the real window. Jump between chapters on the card; Enter moves on and Esc closes.

data.name: Help.QuickStartTip
data.value: Select any row to read its requirements, path and giver in the detail pane. Right-click a row for pin, map flag and journal.

data.name: Help.QuickStartSettingsTip
data.value: Text too small? Settings › General has the window scale, a text size and an icon size.

data.name: Help.PhaseAcceptedMeaning
data.value: In the journal now; the detail pane shows the step.

data.name: Help.PhaseReadyMeaning
data.value: Every requirement is met on the current job; go get it.

data.name: Help.PhaseReadyOtherJobMeaning
data.value: Met on another job; the detail pane names it.

data.name: Help.PhaseDoneThisCycleMeaning
data.value: A repeatable quest already turned in since its last reset: Done today for a daily, Done this week for a weekly.

data.name: Help.PhaseBlockedMeaning
data.value: A requirement is unmet; Status names it in one clause.

data.name: Help.PhaseForeclosedMeaning
data.value: Locked out for good, usually by a choice made in another quest; Status names the cause.

data.name: Help.PhaseUnknownMeaning
data.value: Not evaluated: no snapshot, or data the plugin cannot read for this character.

data.name: Help.ChipStateFormat
data.comment: {0} = state name; a "Shown by" chip in Help › The moon phases.

data.name: Help.HighContrastLegendNote
data.value: Showing the high-contrast glyphs (Settings › Themes › High contrast): each moon carries a mark as well as its shape, and states with the same shape differ clearly in brightness.

data.name: Help.StripeBody
data.value: The thin bar on the left edge of each quest table row repeats the row's state as a pattern, so it reads without colour too: in a greyscale stream, through a colour filter or with colour blindness. Hover the stripe for the state and the pattern's name.

data.name: Help.FillingBody
data.value: Tree nodes, Moonlit kinds, flying zones and the Characters dashboard show a ring that fills clockwise from the top with the completion ratio, around a small moon that fills with it. Even one quest shows a gold pip, and the ring closes only when everything is done. Where the ring is small the number sits beside it. Locked out quests are left out of the total.

data.name: Help.FilterCardBodies.0
data.value: Drops Completed and Locked out quests. Per-category overrides let you hide completed everywhere except, say, the main scenario.

data.name: Help.FilterCardBodies.1
data.value: Keeps only Ready, Ready on another job and In journal: the quests you can act on now. Takes the same per-category overrides.

data.name: Help.FilterCardBodies.2
data.value: All eight phases as checkboxes for fine control. Untick a phase to hide its quests.

data.name: Help.FilterCardBodies.3
data.value: Expansion, Added in (the patch series a quest came with: 7.5x is 7.5, 7.51, 7.55 and the rest, newest first), level range, job category, reward kind (three-state per kind), Repeatable, Seasonal active, Pinned only and Abandoned only narrow the table further; Include removed widens it to quests the game deleted.

data.name: Help.FilterCardBodies.4
data.value: One-click views on the toolbar, with All first to turn them off: Unlocks, My level, Stalled, Story sidequests and Sprout mode; the filter panel keeps the number of days Stalled waits. Unlocks opens with the unlock quests of the newest patch series ("New in 7.5x": 7.5, 7.51, 7.55 and the rest), above a gold line; the detail pane says which patch any quest came with ("Added in 7.5"). Story sidequests lists the sidequests with journal artwork, the ones that tell a small story, zone by zone, with each side story in the order you play it; a book after the name marks them in any view, and its tooltip says which story and how far in ("3 of 9"). The detail pane shows the story's progress as "Story: <first quest> · 3 of 9 done · next: …". The blue aether current quests that open a zone's story lines are part of it; other blue unlock quests (dungeons, systems, jobs) are left out.

data.name: Help.FilterCardBodies.5
data.value: While filters narrow the table, a line of chips sits over the list, one per filter, which the Filters button's number counts; when they do not fit, "+N" lists the rest. Click a chip to clear it; Reset clears them all and the search. The tree scope is in the list's title, with an × to clear it.

data.name: Help.FilterCardBodies.6
data.value: When the table empties, it names the filters responsible as chips: click one to clear only that filter, or Reset filters to clear them all.

data.name: Help.FiltersTip
data.value: Filters, sort and the viewed character are remembered between sessions.

data.name: Help.QuestCardBodies.0
data.value: The first card under the quest's picture: every requirement with ✓ or ✗. The one that blocks you has a gold bar and a gold label; hover a ✗ for the exact gap, such as the rank or level you still need. A "Note:" under the list explains the few quests the game offers anyway.

data.name: Help.QuestCardBodies.1
data.value: The prerequisite chain as a star chart: a moon per quest on a thread that is gold where you have walked and dashed where you have not, one band per expansion. The header says how many quests still stand before this one, and "Next" names the one to do first. Finished stretches fold into a bead ("12 quests done"); click it to open them. Where a quest accepts either of two previous quests, the other way in is a hollow moon beside the thread; click it to see its own path. This quest is the large moon with the halo; when it is scrolled out of view, the "this quest" pill brings it back. Click any step to inspect it.

data.name: Help.QuestCardBodies.2
data.value: Under this quest the thread branches into what it opens once turned in. Click an entry to jump to it.

data.name: Help.QuestCardBodies.3
data.value: Along the bottom of the pane: Flag on map (Teleport instead when Lifestream is installed), then Pin, Show path, Link in chat, Copy coordinates, Open journal and Report, then Walk to giver and Go to giver (with vnavmesh; Stop while moving) and, in the giver's city, an aethernet hop. Every button works from the keyboard; a greyed one says why on hover. The Giver card above names the NPC, the zone and the coordinates.

data.name: Help.QuestCardBodies.4
data.value: The last line says where the state came from: "Checked just now · live" for the character you are logged in as, "From Michiru's snapshot, 2 d ago" for a stored one, or "Log in to check this quest" before the first login.

data.name: Help.QuestCardBodies.5
data.value: For a quest you have completed, the Journal card at the bottom of the pane reads its journal entries as the game wrote them, from the game's own files, with its objectives: Read the journal opens it and Copy entry copies one entry. For a quest in your journal it shows the entries up to the step you are on, never further, and nothing for a quest you have not taken. On the character you are logged in as the text reads as the game showed it to you; on a stored character, words that depend on who reads them show both versions (he/she). Settings › Journal › Search › "Search quest text" (off by default) lets the search box find quests by the words of their journal entries, among the quests the character shown has completed only. The first time, the plugin reads every quest's text in the background (a few seconds) and keeps a word index, not the text, in its config folder; it is rebuilt after a game patch.

data.name: Help.QuestTip
data.value: With no quest selected, the pane shows Tonight: how many quests you can pick up now (Show them filters the table to them), the next main scenario quest and what blocks it, the events running now and your pinned quests that are ready. A table row's right-click menu has pin, map flag, journal, copy name, show path and chat link too.

data.name: Help.UniqueBody
data.value: A Moonlit treasure is a reward that exists nowhere else: an emote, mount, minion, roll, card, duty or feature you can only find on this road. Anything trades, shops or achievements also hand out is not unique. A few rewards the Online Store also sells or a duty also drops stay listed with a "Store only" or "Also drops" mark (hover it for where); tick "Hide rewards found elsewhere" to leave them out of the list and the counts.

data.name: Help.ConfidenceBody
data.value: Each row carries a badge saying how the verdict was reached. Hover a badge in the table for its source.

data.name: Help.ConfidenceCommunityMeaning
data.value: reported by players, not yet checked

data.name: Help.ConfidenceCuratedMeaning
data.value: checked by hand and shipped with the plugin

data.name: Help.HaveBody
data.value: Whether the viewed character owns the reward. Emotes, mounts, minions, rolls, cards and duties are read from the live client, so a stored snapshot shows a dash for them.

data.name: Help.OverridesBody
data.value: Not unique (hide) in a row's context menu removes a quest from Moonlit; Mark as unique in the detail pane adds one. Both act only while Shift or Ctrl is held (or on two clicks, if you chose that under Settings › Advanced › Safety) and save at once. A floating Undo stays for eight seconds, with Add note to name the reward.

data.name: Help.RestoreBody
data.value: Restore shipped verdict, in the row's context menu or the detail pane, undoes either. Hidden quests stay listed under the Yours confidence filter, struck through, so they can be restored; Settings › Characters & data lists every verdict with Restore and Restore all. Overrides live in user/overrides.json and survive updates.

data.name: Help.CharacterCardBodies.0
data.value: Everything read from a character: completed quests, journal, job levels, Grand Company, allied societies and unlocked duties. One per character, refreshed while you play and again on logout.

data.name: Help.CharacterCardBodies.1
data.value: Pick a stored character to browse the catalog as that character. The toolbar's live pip turns hollow and the status bar names the snapshot.

data.name: Help.CharacterCardBodies.2
data.value: Completion per journal section, Moonlit progress, pins, recent activity, job levels by role, Grand Company and society standings.

data.name: Help.CharacterCardBodies.3
data.value: At the bottom: every character's state for the quest selected in the Journal, without switching characters.

data.name: Help.CharacterCardBodies.4
data.value: Export JSON writes the snapshot to the exports folder in the config directory. For a spreadsheet or a collection tracker, Settings › Characters & data › Export (or /tsuki export) writes the completed quests or the Moonlit collection as JSON or CSV, without your name unless you tick Include character name; nothing is ever uploaded. Forget deletes a stored character. Settings can delete everything.

data.name: Help.CharacterCardBodies.5
data.value: A quest that leaves your journal without being completed is listed under Abandoned (N) with the step it had reached and when ("step 3 of 5 · 2 days ago"), with Flag, Teleport and Reveal to go and take it up again; Show in Journal turns on the Abandoned filter. Chat says "Abandoned: [quest] (step 3 of 5)" the moment it happens (Settings › Alerts). Taking the quest up again or completing it clears the row.

data.name: Help.CharacterCardBodies.6
data.value: While a seasonal event runs, Seasonal events lists its quests with their moon, state and giver, and the Todo overlay shows the ones you can start or have in your journal under Event quests running now. At login, chat says "Moonfire Faire is running: 2 quests ready" once per event (Settings › Alerts). An end date appears ("ends Aug 28 (Lodestone)") only when the Lodestone announced it; otherwise it says running now, never a guess. Completed seasonal quests by year keeps your history; the year is the one the Lodestone gave the event, or counted from the nearest announced one.

data.name: Help.CharacterCardBodies.7
data.value: Every quest a character still needs for one thing, in order: the signpost button under a quest (Route to this), Route to this reward in a Moonlit row's menu, and Route to unlock… beside Job quests (or a right-click on a class under Jobs) for a job such as Blue Mage. Each quest comes after the ones it needs, lower levels first where there is a choice; a level gate marks where to level up, main scenario milestones split the list, and where a quest takes either of two earlier quests the shorter way is used and the other is shown with its count. Viewing a stored alt gives that alt's route. Copy route copies it as a Markdown list without your name; Pin all (hold, or Shift or Ctrl and click) pins every step for the Todo overlay, with an Undo.

data.name: Help.CharacterCardBodies.8
data.value: After a break of 14 days or more (Settings › Alerts), a card above the detail pane says what you had in your journal and where each quest stands now, the main scenario then and now, what the game added since by patch series (Show in Journal sets the Added in filter), the events running now and the levels that moved. It waits until every character was away that long, so an idle alt stays quiet, and opens once per session. With no earlier capture it asks when you last played; Since you were away… beside the capture line opens it any time, and Don't show again quiets it for that character.

data.name: Help.FlightCardBodies.0
data.value: Every zone you can fly in, under its expansion, with a halo that fills as you attune its currents; the zone you stand in is marked ● and selected first. Pick a zone and the table lists its quest currents: attuned or not, the quest's state and status, and Flag or Teleport to the giver.

data.name: Help.FlightCardBodies.1
data.value: Quest currents come from quests, five per zone in most expansions, and completing the quest attunes them. Field currents are touched in the world; the tab counts them but never locates them. Use the Aether Compass, a General Action under Actions & Traits, to point at the nearest one.

data.name: Help.FlightCardBodies.2
data.value: /tsuki nearby opens a small window with the quests you can start in the current zone: state moon, level and job. A click on the name shows it in the Journal, a double-click flags the giver on the map, and right-click or … opens Flag, Teleport and Link in chat. Also in your journal here folds out the quests in your journal whose giver stands in the zone. The cog opens its settings in Settings › In game.

data.name: Help.FlightCardBodies.3
data.value: ☾ N in the server info bar is the count of quests you can start here. Hover it for the first five names; click it to open Nearby quests. It hides at zero unless Keep the entry visible is on, and Settings › In game › Nearby and server info bar can turn it off entirely.

data.name: Help.FlightCardBodies.4
data.value: /tsuki zone prints chat links for the quests you can start in the current zone, by level, up to ten. /tsuki which prints every quest the targeted NPC hands out with its state. Both need an evaluated character; the Nearby quests window keeps the same list on screen.

data.name: Help.CommandMeanings.1
data.value: the same, shorter; every subcommand works with any of them, and with your own aliases from Settings › Advanced › Keyboard

data.name: Help.CommandMeanings.2
data.value: search and print matching quests to chat as links; /tsukimichi <text> does the same, and suggests a command when the word was a near miss (Did you mean /tsuki nearby?)

data.name: Help.CommandMeanings.3
data.value: open Settings (/tsukimichi config does the same)

data.name: Help.CommandMeanings.5
data.value: start the guided tour of the window

data.name: Help.CommandMeanings.6
data.value: open the main window on that tab (blues is My blues)

data.name: Help.CommandMeanings.7
data.value: quests you can start in the current zone, as chat links by level

data.name: Help.CommandMeanings.8
data.value: every quest the targeted NPC hands out, with its state

data.name: Help.CommandMeanings.9
data.value: why the selected quest (or the named one) is not offered: its state and blocker, then one line per requirement with met or unmet and the values compared, then the curated note where the game is known to behave differently; a Ready quest says whom to talk to, with a map link. The same list opens in the Journal from an NPC's target-bar menu ("Tsukimichi: quests here")

data.name: Help.CommandMeanings.10
data.value: open the unlock route to the selected (or named) quest: every quest still needed, in order, with where to level up

data.name: Help.CommandMeanings.11
data.value: open or close the Nearby quests window: what you can start in the current zone

data.name: Help.CommandMeanings.12
data.value: show or hide the Todo overlay: pins, Event quests running now, Unlocks you can start here, the next main scenario quest and job quests

data.name: Help.CommandMeanings.13
data.value: copy a diagnostic block for the selected quest (or the named one) to the clipboard, ready to paste into a GitHub issue; the Report button in the detail pane does the same

data.name: Help.CommandMeanings.14
data.value: write the viewed character's completed quests, its Moonlit collection, or both to the exports folder as JSON or CSV (the Settings format when none is named) and print where; see docs/export-format.md. No content id, account or world, and the name only when Settings › Characters & data › Export › Include character name is on

data.name: Help.CommandMeanings.15
data.value: stop every walk, flight, travel chain and hand-off Tsukimichi started (a Questionable run, and the AutoDuty and Artisan runs it began) and say in chat what stopped; put it in a macro for one key. Questionable with a command after stop, and AutoDuty inside a duty, ask first: type it again to confirm

data.name: Help.CommandMeanings.16
data.value: put the caret in the search, while the window has focus

data.name: Help.CommandMeanings.17
data.value: close the open menu or the filter panel; with neither open, close the window

data.name: Help.CommandMeanings.18
data.value: open the focused row's menu in the quest table and the Moonlit list, the same menu a right-click opens; the … button at a row's right end (shown on hover or focus) opens it with a left click

data.name: Help.CommandMeanings.19
data.value: off unless turned on in Settings › Advanced › Keyboard: switch tabs, flag the selected quest's giver, show it in the Journal, pin it. The game sees these keys too: Ctrl+1 to 5 are hotbar 2 by default

data.name: Help.CommandMeanings.20
data.value: back and forward through the quests you looked at, like a browser; the ‹ › buttons at the toolbar's left do the same. The mouse buttons work while the pointer is over the window. The game sees these keys too: turn them off in Settings › Advanced › Keyboard if one is bound there

data.name: Help.CountsCardBodies.0
data.value: Quests the game removed in later patches (the A Realm Reborn trim in 5.3, the Summoner rework, the Crystal Tower rewrite, a few deleted sidequests) sit under the Removed from the game node, off by default, and never count toward any total; a completed one still shows Completed when the node or Include removed reveals it, and its detail pane says which patch removed it where that is known. Quests the game's journal hides but still hands out (So You Want to Be a Gladiator, Leves of Kugane, Sights of the North, the Eureka entry quests, hidden steps of YoRHa and the Resistance Weapons) are filed under the genre their links point at, so a class's quests start with its intro and a zone's sidequests include its leve unlock; the detail pane says which rule filed them. The class intros (So You Want to Be a Gladiator and the other A Realm Reborn classes) are listed but never counted: the class you started as hands you "Way of the …" directly and never offers its intro, so counting it would keep that class one short for good; the job intros (A Dark Spectacle, So You Want to Be a Machinist, What's Your Sign) count as usual. Settings › Advanced › Hidden quest filing › Legacy puts every one of them back in the single bucket releases before 0.6.1 showed.

data.name: Help.CountsCardBodies.1
data.value: A seasonal quest of an event that is not running shows Blocked with "seasonal event not active", and is left out of its genre's total the way a locked-out quest is, so the halo can close without it; it counts again while the event runs. An event whose end date is known and past locks its quests out for good.

data.name: Help.CountsCardBodies.2
data.value: A quest locked out by a choice, such as the other two Grand Companies' quests once you have joined one, is Locked out and left out of the total. A category can reach 100% with them undone, while a wiki's count per genre includes them.

data.name: Help.CountsCardBodies.3
data.value: Unlock quests is not a journal category. It gathers every quest the game draws with the blue + icon, the curated duty and system unlocks, and quests that reward a duty, job, action, trait, aether current or blue magic spell; main scenario and repeatable quests are left out. Its total matches no page of the journal and moves when the curated lists do.

data.name: Help.CountsCardBodies.4
data.value: A daily or weekly quest is one row and one count however many times you have turned it in. Done today or Done this week marks the ones already handed in; they are still counted as completed.

data.name: Help.CountsTip
data.value: The State filter shows locked-out and seasonal quests again; the Removed from the game node and Include removed reveal the deleted ones. Both change the counts while they are on.

data.name: Help.QuirkCardTitles.5
data.value: Game hooks paused after a patch

data.name: Help.QuirkCardBodies.0
data.value: The plugin lists every prerequisite the game's data records. For a few quests the game waives one: Up in Arms is optional once the Zenith is in hand, so what follows it is offered while Tsukimichi still shows Up in Arms undone. The known cases carry a curated note: the detail pane shows it under the requirements as "Note: …", /tsuki why prints it and Report this quest includes it. When an NPC offers a quest shown Blocked here and there is no note, use Report this quest so the exception can be added.

data.name: Help.QuirkCardBodies.1
data.value: Patch 7.0 renamed beast tribes to allied societies and the top rank from Bloodsworn to Allied. Tsukimichi uses the current names, so a requirement reads "Allied" where an older guide, or quest text written before 7.0, says "Bloodsworn". They are the same rank; the quest that awards it carries a note saying so.

data.name: Help.QuirkCardBodies.2
data.value: Patch 7.5 changed the prerequisite of eleven crafter and gatherer sidequests (the Splendorous tools, Cosmic Exploration and the Kugane, Crystarium, Old Sharlayan and Tuliyollal scrip exchanges among them) from Go West, Craftsman to Inscrutable Tastes, a level 50 quest from Morgayne in Foundation. Tsukimichi follows the current game data, so it lists Inscrutable Tastes where an older guide names Go West, Craftsman; each affected quest carries a note with the patch notes as evidence.

data.name: Help.QuirkCardBodies.3
data.value: A custom delivery client's satisfaction rank, the Delivery Moogle's carrier level and, for a phased seasonal event, the running chapter are judged since 0.6.2: a quest that needs rank 4 with M'naago, carrier level 7 or a chapter that has not opened yet shows Blocked with that reason. Only the seven events whose quests open on different phases (Hatching-tide 2014 among them) are gated by chapter; every other seasonal quest is Ready whenever its event runs, whatever phase the game reports. A character file written by an older version carries none of these values, so its quests read as before until the next capture. The game keeps the event chapter in three places and it is not yet known which one the quest givers follow; the plugin reads the first (GameMain) and writes all three to the Dalamud log, once per character and again whenever an event starts, ends or changes phase, under "[festival probe]". If a chapter gate looks wrong during an event, send that log line with the report.

data.name: Help.QuirkCardBodies.4
data.value: Some past seasonal rewards (minions, emotes, mounts, bardings, orchestrion rolls, ornaments) are sold again on the Online Store, which the game files cannot know. Moonlit says so on the rows the curated list covers; if you find one it does not, open a data correction issue with the store page as evidence.

data.name: Help.QuirkCardBodies.5
data.value: The item tooltip panel, the item and NPC menu entries, the server info bar entry and the Duty Finder unlock hint sit beside the game's own interface, which a patch can move. Each Tsukimichi release records the game version they were tested on; on a newer game patch (a new patch date) they pause until an update is tested there, and a chat line at login and a notice in Settings › In game says so. Hotfixes keep the patch date and do not pause them. The Journal, Moonlit, Characters, Nearby, the Todo overlay and every /tsuki command work as usual. To use the hooks anyway, turn on Settings › Advanced › "Run game panels on an untested patch"; it covers the patch you are on now and its hotfixes, so the next patch pauses them again. If one then draws in the wrong place, turn it off and it stops at once.

data.name: Help.QuirkCardBodies.6
data.value: HaselTweaks' Reveal Duty Requirements shows the names of the quests a padlocked duty needs, in the game's own Duty Finder. Tsukimichi's spoiler shield covers only what Tsukimichi draws, so a main scenario name it hides can still show there; turn that tweak off if you want the names kept back.

data.name: Help.QuirkCardBodies.7
data.value: Simple Tweaks can show how far through the main scenario you are. It counts differently from Tsukimichi (which quests count, and how branches, removed and locked-out quests are treated), so the two percentages rarely match; each is right by its own count. Tsukimichi's is the MSQ pill in the status bar and the Characters dashboard.

data.name: Help.QuirksTip
data.value: A quest in the wrong state that is not one of these? Report this quest in the detail pane copies a diagnostic block with the quest id, the state and every requirement's verdict, and no character identifiers; paste it into a GitHub issue.

data.name: Help.SpoilerCardTitles.0
data.value: Main scenario names ahead of you

data.name: Help.SpoilerCardBodies.0
data.value: A main scenario quest more than a set number of quests past your current one (three by default) reads "Main scenario quest (Lv 83)" everywhere a name prints: the table, the detail pane, the status bar, the Todo overlay, Characters, chat links, Wotsit and the diagnostic block. Search finds it only by that placeholder. Quests you have accepted or completed always show their names. Reveal this name in the detail pane shows one quest's name until the plugin reloads.

data.name: Help.SpoilerCardBodies.1
data.value: A quest's banner art sums up the quest, so it shows only once the quest is in your journal or done; until then the detail pane and the name tooltip show a card saying so.

data.name: Help.SpoilerCardBodies.2
data.value: The Sprout mode quick view in the filter panel keeps the table to the expansions your main scenario has reached, with a count of the quests in your reach, and folds the tree's later sections to their counts.

data.name: Help.SpoilerCardBodies.3
data.value: Settings › Spoilers turns the names or the artwork off, sets how many quests ahead keep their names (0 to 10), and holds an override for the character shown: a character who finished the story can show everything while an alt stays shielded.

data.name: Help.SpoilerCardBodies.4
data.value: Some optional content changes a scene later in the story, and the game never says so. When your main scenario (or, for a few, a side story) reaches such a point and the content is not done, a line appears under the MSQ line on Characters and in the Tonight card: "Before you continue: Finish the Eden raid series first." It names only what to do, never what it changes, and it shows only while that quest is ready or in your journal, never earlier and never after. why? (spoiler) under it tells the reason, only when clicked, and stays open for that character until you close it. Chat says it once per character (Settings › Alerts); Settings › Spoilers › "Before you continue notes" turns the lines and the chat line off. The pairs are curated from player reports; if one looks wrong, open a data correction issue.

data.name: Help.SpoilersTip
data.value: Without a character (or a stored one with no data yet) there is no position to measure from, so every main scenario name after the first quest stays hidden until the first capture.

data.name: Help.Tips.0
data.value: Hide completed plus Available now is the fastest view of what to do next.

data.name: Help.Tips.2

data.name: Help.Tips.3

data.name: Help.Tips.4

data.name: Help.Tips.5
data.value: Scope the tree to a genre and sort by level to run a zone's side quests in order.

data.name: Help.Tips.6
data.value: Reward kind filters are three-state: require, exclude or ignore each kind.

data.name: Help.Tips.7
data.value: The toolbar's pip is filled when live and hollow on a snapshot; hover it for the time.

data.name: Help.Tips.8
data.value: Chat notices for newly available quests are off by default; turn them on in Settings, main scenario excluded.

data.name: Help.Tips.9
data.value: Locked out quests are left out of totals, so a category can reach 100% without them.

data.name: Help.Tips.10
data.value: Settings shows how long each poll takes; 1 s is the default and is safe.

data.name: Help.Tips.11
data.value: Delete all data in Settings removes snapshots, pins and overrides but keeps your settings.

data.value: Choose what Tsukimichi shows while you play: the Todo overlay, chat notices, the server info bar count, item hints and the Duty Finder hint. The card opens above the detail pane.

data.name: Help.TopicLede.WhilePlaying
data.value: What Tsukimichi does beside the game while you play, and where to turn each part on or off.

data.name: Help.PlayCardTitles.1
data.value: Nearby and the server info bar

data.name: Help.PlayCardTitles.2
data.value: Item hints and the item menu

data.name: Help.PlayCardBodies.0
data.value: A small panel that stays on screen: your pins, Event quests running now, unlocks you can start here, the next main scenario quest and job quests, an expansion pinned from My blues and a route you follow. Turn it on with the list button at the foot of the tabs, /tsuki todo or Settings › Overlay & routes. Locked makes it click-through.

data.name: Help.PlayCardBodies.1
data.value: Nearby quests lists what you can start in the zone you stand in, by level, with Flag and Teleport. ☾ N in the server info bar is the same count: hover it for the first names, click it for the list. The marker button at the foot of the tabs and /tsuki nearby open it too; its cog opens its settings, where the count can be hidden.

data.name: Help.PlayCardBodies.2
data.value: Hover an item that a quest rewards and a short line near the cursor names the quest and whether it is done. Right-click the item for "Tsukimichi: quest reward", which opens the quest here. Items a quest asks you to hand in say so too. Settings › In game turns each off.

data.name: Help.PlayCardBodies.3
data.value: Target a quest giver and open the target bar's menu: "Tsukimichi: quests here (N)" opens the Journal on every quest that NPC hands out, Blocked ones with their blocker. /tsuki which prints the same list to chat.

data.name: Help.PlayCardBodies.4
data.value: Select a padlocked duty in the Duty Finder or Raid Finder and a small panel beside the window names the quest that unlocks it, with its moon, what it is waiting for, and buttons to reveal it here or flag its giver. It follows the duty you select, not the one under the mouse, and speaks for the character you are logged in on. It knows the unlocks the game data links, a curated list (the A Realm Reborn and Dawntrail launch dungeons, the Crystal Tower and Shadow of Mhach alliance raids, the Heavensward optional dungeons and more) and Moonlit's duty unlocks; for any other padlocked duty it stays silent rather than guess. If the panel names the wrong quest, or a padlocked duty you know the quest for shows nothing, open a data correction issue with the duty's name. Turn it off in Settings › In game › "Unlock hint in Duty Finder".

data.name: Help.PlayCardBodies.5
data.value: A quest you accepted and then abandoned is remembered: the Characters dashboard lists it with Flag and Teleport, and Show in Journal filters the table to them. A chat line names it once per session (Settings › Alerts), so a mis-click is noticed.

data.name: Help.PlayCardBodies.6
data.value: Route to this under a quest, Route to this reward in Moonlit, Route to unlock beside Job quests and the Duty Finder, and /tsuki route [quest name] list every quest still needed, in order, with where to level up. Copy route and Pin all are in the route window.

data.name: Help.PlayCardBodies.7
data.value: Follow this route in the route window puts its next three steps in the Todo overlay, with Flag next stop. Steps drop off as you turn them in, and a chat line says when the route is done. Your pins are not touched.

data.name: Help.PlayCardBodies.8
data.value: Teleport, the aethernet hop and Walk to giver (Lifestream and vnavmesh) take you to a quest's giver, or Go to giver does all three in one click, with Stop at every step. Nothing moves your character unless you press a button.

data.name: Help.PlayCardBodies.9
data.value: Small panels sit beside the game's own windows: "Worth it?" beside a quest offer (what it unlocks, its Moonlit rewards, its chain step), "What this opened" beside the reward window after a turn-in, and a companion beside the Journal for the selected quest. They never accept, decline or complete anything. Settings › In game turns each off.

data.name: Help.PlayCardBodies.10
data.value: After a turn-in, one chat line counts what it opened ("Opened: 2 unlock quests, 8 side quests") with Show to list them, never naming a quest. Tsukimichi's chat lines end each quest with [Open] [Pin] [Route], and Chat 2 gets "Open in Tsukimichi" on quest and item links. Settings › Alerts and In game turn them off.

data.name: Help.PlayCardBodies.11
data.value: Off by default: a short line under a quest giver's name ("☾ Pinned", "☾ Moonlit reward", "☾ Ready on WHM"), and the game's quest banner when a turn-in gives a Moonlit reward or unlocks a duty. Turn them on in Settings › In game and Settings › Alerts.

data.name: Help.PlayTip
data.value: None of these change the game: they read what the game shows you and draw beside it. After a game patch the parts drawn beside the game's own windows pause until they are tested (Known quirks).

data.name: Help.ToggleOverlay
data.value: Turn the overlay on or off

data.name: Help.TopicLede.Privacy
data.value: Tsukimichi reads your own characters, keeps its files on this PC, and goes online only to download the portrait pack when you ask.

data.name: Help.PrivacyCardBodies.0
data.value: Tsukimichi reads the quests, levels, jobs and unlocks of the character you are logged in as, from the game on this PC, the same things the game shows you. It reads nothing about other players.

data.name: Help.PrivacyCardBodies.1
data.value: Your settings are in Dalamud's pluginConfigs/Tsukimichi.json; everything else stays in the folder beside it, pluginConfigs/Tsukimichi: characters/<id>.json, one snapshot per character, with its completion dates (.dates), accepted and abandoned quests (.accepted, .abandoned) and the Since you were away state (.return) beside it; daily backups (.prev, .prev2); user/pins.json, user/overrides.json and user/discovery.json; cache/ for the journal text search index when it is on; and exports/ (or the folder you chose) when you export. While the game runs, a small .live.json tells a second game client who is logged in.

data.name: Help.PrivacyCardBodies.2
data.value: Tsukimichi never uploads or checks anything online. Its one download is the optional portrait pack, from its own GitHub release, after you confirm it in Settings. The quest data ships inside the plugin, and Dalamud installs updates.

data.name: Help.PrivacyCardBodies.3
data.value: Wiki, GitHub and other links open in your browser only when you click them. The plugin itself fetches nothing.

data.name: Help.PrivacyCardBodies.4
data.value: Questionable, AutoDuty, Artisan, GatherBuddy, Lifestream and vnavmesh get work only when you press one of their buttons. While a Tsukimichi window is open it may ask installed ones for their status (what Questionable is running, Allagan Tools' item counts). Other plugins can ask Tsukimichi for quest states through its IPC (docs/ipc.md).

data.name: Help.PrivacyCardBodies.5
data.value: Forget this character, on a stored character in Characters, deletes that character's files. Settings › Characters & data › Delete all Tsukimichi data removes every snapshot, pin and override and keeps your settings. Uninstalling leaves the folder; delete it to remove everything.

data.name: Help.PrivacyCardBodies.6
data.value: Settings › Advanced › Privacy & trust shows the SHA-256 of the Tsukimichi.dll you are running, with Copy. Each GitHub release lists the same hash beside latest.zip, so you can check the plugin you run is the one built there. docs/privacy.md has the whole statement.

data.value: My blues: clear your unlock quests

data.name: PlanHelpBody
data.value: The My blues tab is every blue unlock quest you have left, by expansion and then zone, zones in the order the story reaches them and quests by level. Each row shows its moon, what it unlocks (Dungeon, Trial, Raid, Alliance raid, Field operation, Job, Allied society, Flying, System, Other; "leads to" when the quest is a step towards it), its status and what blocks it, with Flag and Reveal. Filter by kind, Ready only, or Sprout mode to hide expansions your story has not reached. Copy as checklist puts the list as shown on the clipboard as Markdown, ready for Discord ("- [ ] Hallo Halatali (Lv 20, Western Thanalan) — unlocks: Dungeon: Halatali"), with nothing that names you. Pin to overlay on an expansion shows its Ready unlock quests in the Todo overlay; Settings › Overlay & routes turns that section off. Seasonal event quests are not in the plan.

data.value: Enter or → next · ← back · Esc closes

data.name: Tutorial.OfferKeysHint
data.value: Enter takes the tour · Esc: later

data.name: Tutorial.WelcomeBody
data.value: Tsukimichi shows what you can pick up now, why a quest is locked, and which rewards exist nowhere else. Three short chapters; nothing in the tour changes your game.

data.name: Tutorial.SearchBody
data.value: Type a quest, a reward or an id and the table narrows as you type. Ctrl+F jumps here; the × clears it.

data.name: Tutorial.QuickViewsBody
data.value: Quick views answer the common questions: Unlocks, quests at My level, Stalled ones, Story sidequests and Sprout mode. All turns them off.

data.name: Tutorial.FiltersBody
data.value: Filters opens this drawer over the tree. The badge counts what narrows the table; each chip over the list clears one, and the list's title clears the tree scope with its ×.

data.name: Tutorial.TabsBody
data.value: Journal holds every quest; its badge counts the quests you can pick up now. Moonlit, Characters, Flight and My blues come in the last chapter.

data.name: Tutorial.TreeTitle
data.value: Pick a part of the journal

data.name: Tutorial.TreeBody
data.value: Sections, categories and genres narrow the table. Each ring fills as you complete its quests; a gold count means quests you can accept now.

data.name: Tutorial.TableBody
data.value: Click a header to sort and a row to read it. Right-click a row, or use the … at its end or the Menu key, for pin, map flag and the in-game journal.

data.name: Tutorial.DetailBody
data.value: The tour picked a quest for you: the detail pane stacks cards, requirements first, with the one that blocks you marked. With nothing selected, Tonight shows what you can do now.

data.name: Tutorial.StatusBody
data.value: Status says in one clause what stands between you and a quest: a level, a rank, an earlier quest, or the step you are on.

data.name: Tutorial.LegendBody
data.value: Every state has its own shape, so colour is never needed to tell them apart. Hover a moon anywhere for its name.

data.name: Tutorial.PathBody
data.value: The path is a star chart: earlier quests as moons on a gold thread where walked, finished runs folded into beads, then what this one opens. The bar below flags the giver.

data.name: Tutorial.MoonlitBody
data.value: Moonlit lists quest rewards that exist nowhere else, grouped by kind, with the ones you already own marked.

data.name: Tutorial.CharactersBody
data.value: Each character you log in keeps a snapshot here. Pick one to browse the journal as that character, with a dashboard of its progress.

data.name: Tutorial.FlightBody
data.value: Pick a zone to see its aether current quests, what blocks each one, and where to fly next.

data.name: Tutorial.PlanBody
data.value: My blues lists every blue unlock quest you have left, by expansion and zone, with what each one opens. Copy it as a checklist or pin an expansion to the Todo overlay.

data.name: Tutorial.PlayBody
data.value: The Todo overlay keeps pins and nearby unlocks on screen; Nearby lists what you can start in this zone. These two buttons above Help turn them on and off.

data.name: Tutorial.CompanionsBody
data.value: Optional plugins such as Lifestream, vnavmesh, Questionable and AutoDuty add buttons for travel and duties. Settings › Automation shows which you have and where to get the rest.

data.name: Tutorial.HelpBody
data.value: At the foot of the tabs, the question mark opens the guide, where you can replay this tour, and the cog opens Settings for text size, colours and spoilers.

data.name: Tutorial.FinishBody
data.value: Every quest is a step, and the moon fills as you walk. Reopen this tour from Help or Settings; Help has more on every topic.

data.name: CommandHelp
data.value: Open Tsukimichi. search <text> (or just <text>) prints matching quest links; journal, moonlit, characters, flight and blues open those tabs; tour starts the guided tour; zone lists quests you can start here; which lists the targeted NPC's quests; why [quest name] says what blocks the selected or named quest; route [quest name] opens its unlock route; recap [quest name] reads the story so far, of the main scenario or the named quest's chain; nearby and todo toggle the Nearby quests window and the Todo overlay; report [quest name] copies a diagnostic block for the selected or named quest; export [quests|moonlit] [json|csv] writes your completed quests or Moonlit collection to a file; msq says where you are in the main scenario and next says what to do next, both as plain sentences; go [quest name] travels to the current step of the selected or named quest, else to its giver; stop stops every walk, flight, travel chain and hand-off Tsukimichi started; look <code> previews a shared look in Settings › Themes (nothing applies until you choose Apply); settings (or config) and help open those windows.

data.name: GameOffersCountFormat
data.value: The game's own offers: {0} disagree with Tsukimichi, {1} settle a gate Tsukimichi could not check, {2} Ready quests had no marker in their giver's zone.
data.comment: {0} = quests the game showed that Tsukimichi reads as not available, {1} = Not checked quests the game showed, {2} = Ready quests the game did not show.

data.name: GameOffersTooltip
data.value: Tsukimichi reads the game's available-quest markers and quest offers for the logged-in character and compares them with its own states. A Not checked quest the game shows reads Ready; a disagreement is worth a bug report, and Go with the game is yours to pick. A missing marker is only a hint, since the game hides some markers.

data.name: GameOffersCopyTooltip
data.value: Copies one line per quest where the game's markers or offers and Tsukimichi do not say the same thing, in English, for a bug report.

data.name: ExpAdviceTooltip
data.value: The game gives a quest's EXP to the job you are on when you hand it in. Under Quest Sync the amount follows that job's level; a job at the level cap gets nothing. Class, job and role quests are handed in on a job they take.

data.name: ExpAdviceAllCappedFormat
data.value: Your {0} is at the level cap, and no other job of yours that can take this quest would get its EXP.
data.comment: {0} = current job.

data.name: ExpAdviceNeedsJobNone
data.value: This quest needs another job, and none of yours that takes it is at its level yet.

data.name: ExpLineFormat
data.comment: Detail pane, under the EXP amount. {0} = job abbreviation, {1} = its level, {2} = the EXP it gets.

data.name: ExpLineNoLevelFormat
data.comment: The job's level is not known. {0} = job abbreviation, {1} = the EXP it gets.

data.name: ExpShareFormat
data.comment: After the EXP. {0} = whole percent of what the job's level needs to level up.

data.name: ExpShareUnderOne
data.comment: After the EXP, when it is under 1% of what the level needs.

data.name: ExpCappedClauseFormat
data.comment: {0} = a job at the level cap (abbreviation); it would get 0 EXP.

data.name: ExpLessClauseFormat
data.comment: {0} = the current job, {1} = its level, {2} = the EXP it would get.

data.name: GearsetSwitchJobFormat
data.comment: Pill under the unmet Job requirement. {0} = the job's full name (Culinarian).

data.name: GearsetNoneFormat
data.comment: In place of Switch gearset. {0} = the job's full name (Culinarian).

data.name: JobRequirementDetailFormat
data.comment: The unmet Job requirement. {0} = the job the quest requires, {1} = the job you are on (full names).

data.name: GearsetSwitchTooltipFormat
data.value: Equips your gearset {0}, "{1}" (item level {2}), as /gearset change {0} would. Offered only for quests that need a job you are not on.
data.comment: {0} = gearset number, {1} = its name, {2} = its item level.

data.name: GearsetSwitchBlockedFormat
data.comment: {0} = why the game would refuse (you are in combat, …).

data.name: GearsetSwitchPaused
data.value: game panels and hooks are paused on this game version

data.name: JournalRoomTooltip
data.value: The game holds 30 quests at a time; allied society dailies and levequests are kept apart. Make room groups your journal's quests by what finishing them takes, and marks the ones safe to drop.

data.value: Adds Questionable, AutoDuty and Artisan: they play the quest, the duty or the craft for you.

data.value: Custom: your own mix of buttons, set below. Pick a level to use its buttons instead.

data.name: AutomationButtonQuestionableHint
data.value: Start Questionable, Send to Questionable and the priority items. Stop always shows.

data.name: AutomationButtonAutoDutyHint
data.value: AutoDuty runs the duty with Duty Support or Trust. Stop always shows.

data.name: AutomationButtonArtisanHint
data.value: Hand in rows: Artisan crafts what the quest asks for. A run's Stop stays in the status bar.

data.name: UndoToastAutomationFormat
data.comment: {0} = the level's name.

data.name: AboutAutomationRowHint
data.value: What Tsukimichi does itself, what the rules say, and where players draw the line.

data.name: AboutAutomationDoesBody
data.value: It reads your game to track quests. It never moves, fights or talks for you. Every button that does sends the job to another plugin you installed, and only when you press it.

data.name: AboutAutomationOthersBody
data.value: Lifestream teleports, vnavmesh walks, Questionable plays quests, AutoDuty runs duties with Duty Support or Trust, Artisan crafts.

data.name: AboutAutomationRulesBody
data.value: Third-party tools are against the FINAL FANTASY XIV User Agreement. Square Enix has said it acts on what affects other players, and it can act on any account. No setting here makes automation safe.

data.name: AboutAutomationLineBody
data.value: Most players accept automation in solo content and with NPCs (Duty Support, Trust). They object when it runs in content with other players, or unattended for hours. Tsukimichi stops before a duty with other players unless you change that.

data.name: AboutAutomationMannersBody
data.value: Stay at the keyboard. Answer tells yourself. Keep runs short: Start does one quest unless you choose otherwise.

data.name: AboutAutomationLocalBody
data.value: Nothing you do here leaves your computer.

data.name: AboutAutomationAgreementBody
data.value: Opens the FINAL FANTASY XIV User Agreement on Square Enix's site.
